Thanks for the context, Logan — and thanks Samantha for the snapshot. Below is a proposed approval matrix we can use for short pilots and low-dollar suppliers. This is intended as an operational default so procurement can approve without finance sign-off in most cases.

Proposed No-PO Approval Matrix (v1)
1) Risk classification: only vendors classified as LOW risk in the vendor intake (no SOC/PII access, standardized SaaS, vendor has standing corporate insurance).
2) Monthly spend threshold: <= $3,000/month billed.
3) Cumulative spend cap: <= $9,000 total over the engagement.
4) Duration: Pilot engagements only; max 6 months. Any auto-renewal must convert to a PO or contract.
5) Payment method: card on file or procurement-approved charge card.
6) Documentation: intake form completed + risk snapshot attached. Procurement will update vendor profile with a "No-PO Pilot" flag and the approval record (approver name + date).

Exceptions: Anything above the thresholds or medium/high risk requires procurement + finance approval (Finance ticket / JIRA: PROC-312).

Operational notes: I attached a simple spreadsheet that procurement will use to capture approvals. We'll also add a checkbox to the intake form for "No-PO Pilot" and a short notes field for approver rationale. If Logan and team are good with this, procurement will pilot the workflow and handle Veridian's request today.

Next steps:
- Procurement to approve Veridian as low-risk and flag in vendor profile (marissa) — target: today EOD.
- Log an update to the intake form and confirm billing method.
- If approved, notify Samantha and provide the card/billing instructions.
